submissions.answer:
## Question 1

a)SMJ- yes, complete diversity (MA/NH) & AIC (100k>75k), no AUJ/S-G

IPJ- yes, general (Greiner MA dom) & specific

Venue- yes, 1391b1.

York- determines outcome. State law.

Hanna Scalia- valid and applicable? Art VI says must apply. Using FRCP- valid, does not
enlarge, abridge or modify any substantive right (REA). Applicable, differs from MRCP
in plain language and suit filed after effective date. Federal law.

Ginsburg SG- valid and applicable? Art VI says must apply. Valid, see above.
Applicable, argue no: technically don't differ. FRCP less restrictive, don't say you can file

after 2 years, only that you can't after 3. State interest in encouraging timely and better
litigation. State law.

Harlan- affects primary conduct. Could make people more reckless if tort litigation is
harder. State law.

All in all, use state law and dismiss, unless Scalia.

603459 603459

b)Stevens- state law "part of a State's framework of substantive rights or remedies"? MA
limited the scope of rights of pet owners through SoL. State law.

c)The court should rule under the Stevens framework and use state law. Stevens's view
preserves the state law autonomy that our federal government demands. FRCP are not
passed democratically, but they nevertheless can affect effectively substantive issues in
states.

The forum-shopping concern favors state law: a defendant would remove to federal court
if they can win on SoL. This results in a) unnecessarily greater case-load for federal
courts, and b) federal courts applying substantive state law they are unfamiliar with. This
also privileges parties with savvier lawyers who know to remove.

Federal courts don't have strong incentive to create uniformity with respect to clear issues
like SoL: it's easily applied (yes-or-no) and unlikely to greatly affect efficiency.

-------------------------------------------

603459 603459

-------------------------------------------

## Question 2

Class actions are sometimes useful to promote access to justice.

Class actions can help mitigate the Supreme Court's reluctance to require civil counsel.
Individuals without resources to hire lawyers may find representation in a class action
suit. The preclusory effect of class actions will usually not detrimentally affect people
who did not have the resources to litigate anyway. Lawyers representing a class have an
incentive to find as many plaintiffs as possible, putting the onus on legal professionals to
give representation. Furthermore, the individually small amounts often at issue in class
action suits are much more important to lower-income people; giving another avenue for
their recovery disproportionately benefits them.

Take the case of a cell-phone company exploiting contract-unsavvy individuals with a
hidden fee of $20/month. $20/month can be crucial to many people, especially
accumulated over time, but they could never practically sue for it. If they join a class
action, they can get compensation with little personal sacrifice, and the exploitative
contracting practice might be stopped.

Class actions, however, are imperfect. They're very costly, leading to profit-maximization
rather than justice-maximization. Furthermore, class actions are unsuitable for many

603459 603459

important types of disputes, e.g. employment discrimination. In a case like Walmart,
where case-to-case employment discrimination inherently lack commonality of facts, the
class action fails precisely where it's most needed. Finally, considering justice as

procedural as well as a substantive outcome, a class action does not give plaintiffs control
over their own suit, e.g. in decisions to settle.

In an increasingly corporate world, class actions give individuals greater legal leverage
and ease access to representation against large, powerful defendants. Although class
actions are an imperfect tool, they are a healthy evolution of the legal system in response
to enormous wealth/power disparity and increasing systematically caused injuries.

-------------------------------------------

603459 603459

-------------------------------------------

## Question 3

Remand likely for lack of SMJ. No 1331 AUJ, no federal issue; no substantial/disputed
Smith-Grable embedded issue. 1332 diversity: neither defendant citizen of TX (state-
court suit), so if DJ, removal okay. Complete diversity, plaintiff diverse from defendants
(Groucho-TX, Zeppo-DE, Sylvania-DE/OK). Zeppo meets AIC (250k>75k), but Sylvania
doesn't (50k<75k). No 1367: diversity suit, cannot use SJ for Sylvania joined by R20.
With prompt motion, remand also possible for procedural defect- if not all defendants
signed petition or not filed within 30 days of service.

12b MtD:
SMJ: see above, no DJ bc of Sylvania AIC.
IPJ: yes.

Sylvania-
General- no. Not incorporated/principal place of business in TX. Not really at home in
TX, majority of business outside of US. Daimler. No consent nor tag.
Specific- yes. TX has long-arm. Minimal contact between Sylvania/forum/subject
matter-- Sylvania does business in TX, despite no solicitation. McGee. Avails self of
privileges of TX w/ servers. Possibly offends traditional notions of fair play and
justice(Intl Shoe), see Daimler court denying IPJ over largely non-US business.
Distinguishable here, subject matter of suit tied to Texas.

603459 603459

4k1a, federal piggy-backs state IPJ.

Zeppo-

General- yes, DE dom. No substantial and systematic contacts with TX (Daimler).
Specific- yes. Texas has long-arm. Minimal contacts-- availed self of privilege of
conducting activity in TX by driving through(McGee), alleged theft in TX too. Does not
offend traditional notions of fair play and justice- evidence/witnesses in TX, e.g. Chico,
TX wants to provide redress for citizens. Zeppo drives all over, capable of traveling.

Venue- yes.
1391b1- no for Zeppo, doesn't reside in TX. Sylvania yes- not incorporated/PPoB in TX,
but court can exercise IPJ over Sylvania.
1391b2- Zeppo, yes. Substantial part of events in San Antonio-- login theft.
Sylvania probably yes-- unclear where item is (see below), but login info theft probably
substantial event for Sylvania claim. Substantial part of property is situated in server in

1391b3- no. Venue exists elsewhere for both (Zeppo-DE 1391b1, Sylvania-DE/OK
1391b1, NDTX 1391b2).

No information on pleading for 12b6.

Transfer: unlikely.
WDTX happy, IPJ & venue. No FSC. No necessary transfer upon motion.
Private/public interests:

603459 603459

Texas 2R, federal court uses state court's HCOL (Klaxon). Unclear where tort completed,
item arguably partly in MA, TX, and SC. Login info in Dallas, but Groucho still had
access to item even after login stolen, even if Groucho lost exclusive access. Could argue

that once split into three interdependent pieces, item did not exist solely anywhere, so
look to last place the item unambiguously did exist in one place- South Dakota. This was
prior to time of theft, however.

If court doesn't buy SD argument, likely TX- equal share of data in Texas (1/3rd) and
most significant relationship to events under §6 likely Texas. All states may have interest
in protecting assets stored in servers in their jurisdiction, but Texas has additional interest
in protecting citizens.

If HCOL=> TX law, WDTX applying own law. Transfer under 1404 then unlikely.
Access to witnesses in TX (Chico) and Groucho resides in San Antonio.

Federal court can't transfer to state, only federal-federal, so no 1631 transfer to cure SMJ

defect.

603459 603459

## Question 4

IPJ- no change.
SMJ- diversity now possible, Sylvania suit independently has 1332 jurisdiction w/ AIC
met (100k>75k), R20 joinder and no 1367 SJ necessary. Still no 1331.
Venue- no change.

No grounds for dismissal. Transfer unlikely.

## Question 5
Transfer candidates: states where suit might have been brought, i.e. happy court
(Hoffman). SMJ doesn't matter, all 1332.

Happy court in WDTX, so use transferor COL rules (Texas 2R).

WDTX: happy court, see above. Most convenient for Groucho. Connection between
state, controversy and evidence here.

NDTX: IPJ for Sylvania, see above. Possibly IPJ for Zeppo, due to stealing data housed

If TX HCOL decides on TX law, probably transfer to SDTX (most convenient, applying

603459 603459

## Question 6

Appellate jurisdiction: likely not.

District court had SMJ.

FRCP 54- no, multiple claims but no final judgments entered, nor express determination
of no just reason for delay.
1292a1- no, suing for damages not injunction.
1292b- no, no order stating substantial grounds for difference in opinion.
Cohen Exception- unlikely. Transfer order is collateral to merits, is final with respect to
this issue. Transfer itself is non-discretionary, but the court to which it's transferred is not;

discretionary decision is what at's issue for Groucho. Not effectively unreviewable later,
except insofar as it forces Groucho to travel to Delaware, but unlikely to show some

Writ of mandamus- unlikely. No real irreparable harm, clear indisputable right to relief.
Cheney. Granting writ because someone didn't like a state would flood CoA.

If AJ, court would use abuse of discretion SoR if reviewing judge's particular choice of

603459 603459

venue (DE) but de novo SoR if reviewing judge's decision that transfer required (happy

## Question 7

Answer may depend on HCOL analysis:
Arguable that damage calculation methods (comparative v contributory) is procedural or

If procedural, forum law: comparative.

If substantive, 1R HCOL analysis from above (Klaxon).

Summary Judgment:

2. movant entitled to JAMOL

trier of fact could find that Groucho didn't fail to exercise due care in a way that

603459 603459

Celotex: affirmative defense, so Sylvania has burden of persuasion.
Sylvania burden to produce evidence showing-
Negligent in a) choosing too easy a password AND negligent in b) displaying it; or,
Negligent in c) choosing not to enable 2FA.
Engineer memo shows a) and c), Chico deposition shows b). Drawing all reasonable

not a failure to exercise due care

If damage calculation is procedural, Texas law is used, or judge determines not using 2Fa

603459 603459

not a failure to exercise due care, no SJ.

## Question 8

Judge Marcal ordered final judgment to be entered and expressly stated "there is no just
reason for delay," so Groucho has sufficient notice. Groucho may argue, however, that

(large/liquidated claim, financial hardship, expect long time for pending claims).

Sylvania could argue that being held up in suit damages reputation resulting in financial
loss, and that negligence elements not meaningfully connected with Zeppo's conversion
suit.

Likely incorrect use of 54(b), but abuse of discretion SoR is quite deferential.

Issue Preclusion:
Rendering court federal court sitting in diversity; subsequent court is state court. Use the
law of court in which rendering court sits. Semtek.
Because WDTX happy, treat the transfer as merely change in courtroom; unclear,
probably TX COL. Preclusion procedural so still use DE law.

603459 603459

DE follows federal preclusion law: more than one independent basis for a decision and
unclear which used, no issue preclusion. Russell. Two independent, separable theories

causal factor. Sylvania would otherwise be able to use, as this is NMDCOE. Groucho

If TX law: TX preclusion law doesn't follow Russell- two independent theories, can issue

Claim preclusion: DE claim preclusion law, see above.

1. Prior suit against Sylvania proceeded to judgment that was both final and on the merits.
2. Arguable it concerns same transaction & occurrence. Different item stolen, now

603459 603459

because different item lost. Probably not same transaction and occurrence.
3. Groucho plaintiff in both suits.

No claim preclusion because different transaction/occurrence.

feedback.headline: Strong on appealability and preclusion; a venue error propagates into four later answers
feedback.overview: Your best work here is analysis rather than coverage. Question 6 walks every route to interlocutory review — 1291, Rule 54(b), 1292(a)(1), 1292(b), the collateral order doctrine, mandamus — and closes each with a reason. Question 8 finds the analytical heart of the issue preclusion half in the two independent grounds problem, and keeps claim preclusion in its own run. Question 3's citizenship, amount-in-controversy split, and 1367(b) bar are precise. The damage is concentrated in venue. You found a substantial part of the events in San Antonio when the Chico meeting and the server sit in Dallas, in the Northern District. That conclusion empties Question 4, sends Question 5 to a district with no connection to the case, and contradicts your own Question 7. Separately, the location of the incorporeal artwork — the pivot of a twelve-point question — is not worked anywhere on the page.

strengths.label: All four Erie tests applied, not merely named
strengths.detail: Each test gets a bottom line, and the Ginsburg reading does independent work: treating the federal rule as fixing only an outer three-year boundary is the narrowing move the course teaches, not a restatement of Scalia.
strengths.answerExcerpt: FRCP less restrictive, don't say you can file after 2 years, only that you can't after 3.

strengths.label: Stevens run efficiently on a two-point subpart
strengths.detail: You used the planted fact — Massachusetts put the two-year limit in the statute creating the pet cause of action — to make the as-applied Rules Enabling Act argument. That is the whole point of the subpart, and it cost you two sentences.
strengths.answerExcerpt: MA limited the scope of rights of pet owners through SoL.

strengths.label: All three required components, with specifics
strengths.detail: The $20-per-month hidden-fee example is a genuine negative-value claim, and you used Wal-Mart's commonality problem rather than gesturing at its holding. That specificity is what a policy answer earns credit for.
strengths.answerExcerpt: case-to-case employment discrimination inherently lack commonality of facts

strengths.label: Subject matter jurisdiction run cleanly
strengths.detail: Citizenship for all three parties, the amount-in-controversy split, and the 1367(b) bar on a plaintiff's claim against a Rule 20 co-defendant in a diversity case. You did not reach for the reading that would let the deficient claim ride along.
strengths.answerExcerpt: No 1367: diversity suit, cannot use SJ for Sylvania joined by R20.

strengths.label: Every route to interlocutory review closed with a reason
strengths.detail: You did not stop at finality. The collateral order elements are each addressed, mandamus is taken seriously and rejected on exigency, and the standards of review are split by the type of question reviewed rather than given as one label.
strengths.answerExcerpt: Not effectively unreviewable later, except insofar as it forces Groucho to travel to Delaware

strengths.label: Summary judgment burden placed on the movant carrying the trial burden
strengths.detail: You saw that Sylvania moves on its own affirmative defense, mapped each exhibit to each theory of negligence, and held that a failure of memory does not rebut the 2FA ground.
strengths.answerExcerpt: Celotex: affirmative defense, so Sylvania has burden of persuasion.

strengths.label: Two independent grounds identified as the decisive problem
strengths.detail: Finding that the judge never said which ground carried her ruling, and running that through Delaware's federal preclusion law, is the core of the issue preclusion half. You also noticed that the changed password removes that theory from the second suit.
strengths.answerExcerpt: more than one independent basis for a decision and unclear which used, no issue preclusion. Russell.

improvements.label: Question 1(a): show the arithmetic, and cut the threshold run nobody asked for
improvements.whatHappened: The answer opens with SMJ, IPJ, and venue for the suit against Professor Greiner. Question 1 asked for none of that. The outcome-determinative conclusion is then asserted without the dates that create the conflict.
improvements.whyItMatters: The conflict exists only because an August 2022 filing falls between the two-year and three-year marks after a December 2019 injury. One clause showing that turns York from a label into a demonstration. The Harlan run is also one-sided: the course's counterpoint is that a limitations period governs when lawyers file, not how clients plan.
improvements.howToImprove: Delete the opening SMJ, IPJ, and venue lines. Spend those words on the date arithmetic, on the contrary Harlan argument, and on the three words missing from your validity recitation — really regulates procedure.

improvements.label: Question 1(c): the strongest argument against your position is absent
improvements.whatHappened: Three justifications are on the page, but separation of powers is not. Your claim that the federal rules are not passed democratically goes unanswered.
improvements.whyItMatters: Congress's power to constitute the lower federal courts, combined with the Necessary and Proper Clause and the delegation in the Rules Enabling Act, is the best case for applying Rule 87. Meeting it converts your position from a preference into an argument.
improvements.howToImprove: Trim the removal scenario, which this fact pattern does not present, and use those words to state the delegation argument and then answer it.

improvements.label: Question 3: run 1391 against the district map, in order
improvements.whatHappened: You found a substantial part of the events in San Antonio while noting in the same passage that the server sits in the Northern District. The Chico meeting in Dallas is never assigned to a district at all.
improvements.whyItMatters: Venue is a brain-off topic: walk the enumerated bases mechanically against the geography the exam supplies. This conclusion carried into Questions 4, 5, 7, and 8.
improvements.howToImprove:
Take the bases in statutory order.
1. 1391(b)(1): where does each defendant reside — Zeppo in Delaware, Sylvania where it is subject to personal jurisdiction.
2. 1391(b)(2): name the district for each event — the Chico meeting is Dallas, which is the Northern District, and the servers are Northern District of Texas, Massachusetts, and South Carolina.
3. 1391(b)(3): reach it only if nothing qualifies above.
Pay for this with the 1404 convenience and choice-of-law discussion, which the prompt expressly told you to skip.

improvements.label: Question 3: remand only the claim that lacks jurisdiction
improvements.whatHappened: The answer treats Sylvania's amount-in-controversy shortfall as defeating diversity for the whole case.
improvements.whyItMatters: The Zeppo claim independently satisfies 1332 at $250,000. Sending everything back gives away a claim that belongs in federal court, and the scope of the remand is the graded point.
improvements.howToImprove: Replace the broader no-diversity line with the split as your holding: the Sylvania claim is remanded, the Zeppo claim stays.

improvements.label: Question 4: venue is the whole question and it gets two words
improvements.whatHappened: "Venue- no change," then "No grounds for dismissal. Transfer unlikely." Six words on a five-point question.
improvements.whyItMatters: Filing originally rather than removing puts venue squarely in play, and it fails: Zeppo resides in Delaware, and the Chico meeting and the servers are in the Northern District. Once venue is improper the court has no discretion to keep the case, which is also what sets up Question 5.
improvements.howToImprove: Run 1391(b)(1) and then (b)(2) against the geography, state that venue is improper, and say the consequence is mandatory dismissal or transfer. The words come from personal jurisdiction, which you can correctly leave as a cross-reference.

improvements.label: Question 5: the chosen destination has no connection to the case
improvements.whatHappened: The answer lists the Western District of Texas as a transfer candidate and then picks the Southern District of Texas.
improvements.whyItMatters: A court cannot transfer to itself, and the Southern District appears nowhere in these facts. Naming the most likely destination is half of a five-point question, so an unsupported pick loses the half.
improvements.howToImprove: Test each candidate for personal jurisdiction over each defendant and for proper venue, then rule the losers out by name: no jurisdiction over Sylvania in the Southern District of California or South Dakota, none over Zeppo in Massachusetts, the Western District of Oklahoma, or South Carolina. That leaves Delaware and the Northern District of Texas, and you choose between them on convenience. Cut the repeated "unclear where tort completed" passage to fund it.

improvements.label: Question 7: locate the item, with reasons
improvements.whatHappened: South Dakota and Texas appear as candidate sources of law, but the answer never works out where the incorporeal artwork was at the time of the theft.
improvements.whyItMatters: On a twelve-point question the location is the pivot: it decides whether the negligence finding bars recovery outright or only reduces it. A three-part list of contingencies stands in for the analysis that would resolve them.
improvements.howToImprove: Canvass the candidates with a reason for and against each — Pierre, where the account was opened; San Antonio, the owner's home; Oklahoma or Delaware, tied to the company; and the three server states, where the code physically sat. Pick one and carry it to the contributory-versus-comparative consequence. Fund this by trimming the opening substance-versus-procedure passage, which ends without resolving anything.

improvements.label: Question 7: the choice-of-law step contradicts your own Question 5
improvements.whatHappened: Question 5 states the happy-court rule and applies transferor Texas rules under the Second Restatement. Question 7 then cross-references "above" for a First Restatement analysis. Both cannot be right.
improvements.whyItMatters: The premise is what failed. The happy-court rule turns on whether the transferor court had personal jurisdiction and proper venue; venue in the Western District was improper, so nothing follows the transfer and Delaware's own First Restatement rules govern. Klaxon supplies only the general proposition that a federal court uses the choice-of-law rules of the state where it sits.
improvements.howToImprove: Fix the premise once, in Question 5, and carry the same conclusion into Questions 7 and 8 (Ferens). Then delete the "from above" cross-reference and name Delaware and the First Restatement directly.

improvements.label: Question 7: you applied the right principle to one ground and not the other
improvements.whatHappened: Testimony that Groucho does not remember his password practices is treated as creating a genuine dispute on the password ground. One line later, the same kind of testimony is correctly treated as no evidence on the 2FA ground.
improvements.whyItMatters: An absence of memory is an absence of evidence, not contradictory evidence. The contradiction undercuts the burden-shifting you built carefully.
improvements.howToImprove: Apply the same holding to both grounds in the clause you already wrote for the 2FA theory. It costs nothing and removes a visible inconsistency.

improvements.label: Question 8: name the question as intersystem preclusion
improvements.whatHappened: "Because WDTX happy, treat the transfer as merely change in courtroom; unclear, probably TX COL. Preclusion procedural so still use DE law." Two frameworks are mixed, and Delaware is reached by the wrong route.
improvements.whyItMatters: This is intersystem preclusion, not choice of law — that term is reserved for horizontal and vertical choice of law. Calling preclusion procedural is not the course's path to the answer.
improvements.howToImprove: Replace the three clauses with one: venue in the Western District was improper, so no transferor rules carry over, and the rendering court is a federal court sitting in Delaware, which follows federal preclusion law. Then run Russell as you already do.

improvements.label: Question 8: state the floor, and drop the non-mutual label
improvements.whatHappened: The answer never says that the Oklahoma court must give at least the preclusion the rendering system would, and may choose to give more. It also describes the posture as non-mutual defensive preclusion.
improvements.whyItMatters: The floor is what makes your Texas-law alternative branch coherent — extra preclusion is Oklahoma's option, not its obligation. And the parties are identical in both suits, Groucho against Sylvania, so mutuality is present and nothing here is non-mutual.
improvements.howToImprove: Add one clause on the floor and strike the non-mutual characterization. Also isolate the 2FA failure as the only issue common to both suits before you reach the two-grounds problem, since you already spotted that the password facts changed.

revisionPlan: Redo Question 3's venue section by walking 1391(b)(1), then (b)(2), then (b)(3), placing each event in its actual judicial district before drawing any conclusion.
Rewrite Question 4 as a venue answer: improper in the Western District, so dismiss or transfer, with personal jurisdiction left as a cross-reference.

Rebuild Question 5 by testing each candidate district for personal jurisdiction over each defendant and for venue, ruling out the losers by name, then choosing between Delaware and the Northern District of Texas on convenience.
In Question 7, state that the transferor venue was improper so Delaware's First Restatement rules govern, and delete the cross-reference to the Second Restatement analysis.
In Question 7, canvass the possible locations of the incorporeal artwork with a reason for each, pick one, and carry it through to whether recovery is barred or reduced.
In Question 8, replace the choice-of-law language with the intersystem preclusion route and add that the rendering court's law sets a floor.
feedback.exampleRevision:
